themes_detail.label: Illegal Posting Explosion
themes_detail.summary: Illegal posting complaints spiked to 11 THIS WEEK versus a baseline of 0.1 per week over the prior 8 weeks—an 8,700% increase (z-score: 32.88)—suggesting a coordinated campaign or sudden enforcement gap in Flatlands/Canarsie.
evidence: 11 illegal posting complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Z-score of 32.88 indicates extreme statistical anomaly
No prior week in 90-day period approached this volume
reporting_angles: Is this a coordinated poster campaign by a specific entity (political, commercial, or protest-related)?
Did 311 enforcement or community reporting suddenly change, or did illegal posting itself accelerate?

themes_detail.label: Street & Sidewalk Noise Surge
themes_detail.summary: Street and sidewalk noise complaints jumped to 24 THIS WEEK, up 368% from the 8-week baseline of 5.1 per week (z-score: 3.93), indicating a sudden spike in outdoor disruption—construction, events, or street activity.
evidence: 24 street/sidewalk noise complaints THIS WEEK vs. 5.1 weekly average
Temporal clustering suggests new source or event, not background noise
reporting_angles: What construction, street fairs, or commercial activity began this week?
Are nighttime noise ordinances being enforced in Flatlands/Canarsie?

themes_detail.label: Vehicle & Residential Noise Cluster
themes_detail.summary: Vehicle noise complaints rose 200% last week (12 vs. 4.0 weekly baseline), while residential noise remains elevated at 902 total complaints over 90 days—a multi-layered noise problem affecting quality of life.
evidence: 12 vehicle noise complaints last week vs. 4.0 weekly average (z-score: 3.08)
902 residential noise complaints over 90 days indicates sustained problem
Two noise categories spiking suggests systematic issue, not isolated incident
reporting_angles: Are illegally modified vehicles or street racing occurring in specific neighborhoods?
Is parking enforcement being used to discourage overnight idling and noise?

themes_detail.label: Hazardous Materials & Boiler Failures
themes_detail.summary: Hazardous materials complaints spiked 567% three weeks ago (5 vs. 0.8 weekly baseline, z-score: 5.13), and boiler complaints rose 700% same period (3 vs. 0.4 baseline, z-score: 5.42)—possible chemical release or widespread heating system failures.
evidence: 5 hazardous materials complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 0.8 weekly baseline (567% spike)
3 boiler complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 0.4 weekly baseline (700% spike)
Simultaneous spikes suggest possible environmental event or seasonal heating crisis
reporting_angles: Was there an industrial chemical spill or transportation accident three weeks ago?
Are landlords failing to maintain boilers ahead of winter—creating a heating crisis?

themes_detail.label: Elevator & Building Safety Issues
themes_detail.summary: Elevator complaints jumped 220% last week (8 vs. 2.5 weekly baseline, z-score: 2.84), coupled with 357 recent DOB building permit filings including 265 alterations—suggests ongoing building code violations or deferred maintenance in aging structures.
evidence: 8 elevator complaints last week vs. 2.5 weekly average (z-score: 2.84)
357 building permits filed in last 90 days (265 alterations) indicates significant construction activity
High alteration volume may reflect poor code compliance or catch-up repairs
reporting_angles: Are alterations being filed reactively after elevator failures rather than proactively?
Which buildings have repeated elevator violations, and are landlords being held accountable?
